notes:
Shopify store. robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow and no full-site block; Tier-1 direct HTTP (curl + Shopify sitemap/products.json/search-suggest.json endpoints) was sufficient and fully reliable, so Tiers 2/3 were not needed. Fetched sitemap.xml -> sitemap_collections_1.xml, which enumerates all 509 live collections. Filtered for holiday/festival/occasion-named handles and found a large set of candidates: diwali, christmas-day, christmas-collection, christmas-sale, christmas-lookbook, new-year, new-year-sale, new-year-lookbook, fathers-day, mothers-day, raksha-bandhan, lohri, lohri-sale, bhai-dooj, navaratri, eid, republic-day, republic-day-sale, independence-day, independence-day-sale, valentines-day, valentines-day-sale, valentines-lookbook, friendship-day, holi-sale, holi-lookbook (no plain 'holi' collection exists), plus gifts/special-occasion/everyday-occasion hub pages. No collections at all exist for halloween, easter, or thanksgiving (confirmed absent from the full collection list and via site search-suggest.json, which returned zero results for 'santa', 'rangoli', 'rakhi', 'pooja', and zero for any halloween/easter/thanksgiving query).

Content-verified every plausible holiday candidate via /collections/<handle>/products.json (bypassing the capped on-page count) instead of trusting titles/URLs, per the Mother's-Day false-positive precedent:
- diwali (139 products), lohri (139), new-year (139) returned byte-identical product-ID sets.
- eid (142), navaratri (142), bhai-dooj (142) returned byte-identical product-ID sets (a 3-item superset of the diwali/lohri/new-year set).
- mothers-day (119), raksha-bandhan (119), valentines-day (119), friendship-day (119) returned byte-identical product-ID sets.
- fathers-day (126) and republic-day/independence-day (64 each, identical to each other) were likewise generic, undifferentiated decor sets.
- christmas-day and christmas-collection (72 each) were also byte-identical to each other.
Sampled full product listings and per-product tags for the diwali set: every item (brass tissue holders, crystal chandeliers, pendant/wall/outdoor lights, lanterns, candle holders, decorative jars) carries the SAME broad tag stack simultaneously - e.g. one lantern is tagged Bhai Dooj + Christmas Collection + Diwali + Eid + Garden Lanterns all at once; another is tagged Diwali + Eid + Lohri + Navaratri + New Year at once. No item is occasion-exclusive. Meta descriptions confirm the pattern is generic gifting SEO copy, not curated merchandise, e.g. /collections/diwali: 'Buy/Send Diwali gifts online in India... wide range of products for diwali sale' and /collections/fathers-day: 'Buy/Send gifts for father... wide range of gifts to father. Shop now and get 20% off' - both describing the same generic decor catalog reframed per occasion.
Site search-suggest.json (the store's own search layer) returned ZERO results for diya, rangoli, rakhi, pooja, and santa, confirming the catalog contains no actual Diwali-specific (diyas/rangoli/torans-as-decor-items - 'toran' only matched an unrelated 'Toran Two Tiered Serving Stand', a generic serving tray with no festive meaning), Rakhi-specific, or Christmas-ornament-specific SKUs anywhere on the site; the retailer sells lighting/brass/lantern/vase home decor and reuses that single catalog across dozens of occasion-named URLs (also including Anniversary, Birthdays, Housewarming, Thank You, Get Well Soon, Grand Opening, Thinking of You, Love & Romance) as a gifting-navigation/SEO layer, not genuine occasion-curated PLPs.
All '-sale' variants (diwali-sale, christmas-sale, new-year-sale, holi-sale, valentines-day-sale, lohri-sale, republic-day-sale, independence-day-sale) and all '-lookbook' variants (christmas-lookbook, new-year-lookbook, valentines-lookbook, holi-lookbook) were additionally excluded on independent grounds (storewide sale/clearance and editorial-lookbook pages per the boundary rules), on top of failing the same generic-catalog content check.
Conclusion: no genuine seasonal/holiday category exists on this site under any tested criterion - every festival/occasion-labeled collection resolves to the same reused, non-occasion-specific decor catalog. Diwali, Christmas, New Year, Holi, Raksha Bandhan, Eid, Lohri, Navaratri, Bhai Dooj, Father's/Mother's Day were all specifically checked and rejected on content-verification grounds; Halloween, Easter, Thanksgiving, and Valentine's Day were checked and are structurally identical (rejected) or entirely absent from the taxonomy.
